ideas: What the object is and where it came from
The memory or person connected to it
Why you've never thrown it away

phrases.meaning: give to a younger family member
a valuable item passed through generations

model: The object I've kept the longest is an old wristwatch that my grandfather gave me when I finished high school, which was about nine years ago. It's a simple silver watch with a white face and a brown leather strap. My grandfather bought it in the nineteen seventies, when he was a young teacher, and he wore it every single day for over thirty years. When I passed the university entrance exam, he called me into his room, took the watch off his wrist and put it in my hand. He said that time was the most important thing a student had. I remember I was too emotional to say anything. The watch isn't expensive, and honestly it doesn't even keep perfect time anymore. The strap was completely worn out, so I replaced it a few years ago. But it has huge sentimental value for me, especially because my grandfather passed away the year after. Every time I look at it, it brings back memories of his small house and the smell of his green tea. I don't wear it to work, because I'm scared of breaking it, but I keep it in a box on my desk. I really treasure it, and I'll always hold on to it, because I could never part with it. One day I'd like to hand it down to my own children, so it becomes a real family heirloom.
